transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-21
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Mills (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Evelyn Park (Head of ML, Lodestar), Marcus Lee (VP Eng), Aisha Khan (Infra Lead), Tom Reynolds (Procurement)

Summary: quick discovery focused on dedicated/reserved capacity for Lodestar's inference workloads. Customer is evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private; heavy emphasis on isolation, predictable throughput, burst capability, and cost tradeoffs. Agreed next steps include pricing, security docs, and a benchmark pilot.

Topics: dedicated capacity sizing, isolation (network/KMS), burst/burstback, autoscaling policies, latency vs cost, quantization and batching, rollout plan and timeline, procurement constraints.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. This is Jordan from Redwood, AE on the account. We have Priya and Diego from SEs also on the call. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Evelyn: Good, thanks. Evelyn here. Appreciate you taking the time.
[00:10] Marcus: Marcus, hi.
[00:12] Aisha: Aisha.
[00:13] Tom: Tom, procurement. Quick logistics - I might drop if another meeting overlaps.
[00:16] Jordan: No worries. Quick agenda - 1) Understand your current stack and latency/cost needs, 2) talk through dedicated cluster options and isolation, 3) discuss burst and scaling expectations, 4) agree next steps. Sound good?
[00:24] Evelyn: Yep. We are evaluating whether hosted makes sense for initial launch or we go dedicated from day one. Our main concerns: data isolation for PII, predictable latency under peak, and keeping unit cost reasonable.
[00:35] Priya: Thanks. Can you give us a bit of background - models you plan to run, typical sequence lengths, and concurrency/throughput targets?
[00:42] Evelyn: Sure. For core product features - document summarization, Q&A over customer docs, and chat assistant. We're using a mix: some open models fine-tuned in-house, plus a couple of larger public models for research. Primary model in production will be a 34B transformer variant (we call it lodestar-34b internally), typical input length is 256-1024 tokens, average 320 tokens, but some long context calls up to 4k.
[01:05] Marcus: For traffic, our current pre-prod tests show average 120 qps at peak during internal load tests, but we expect production peaks around 350 qps during pushes. Latency SLO is 90th percentile under 250 ms for the short prompts; for long contexts we accept higher but want predictability.
[01:25] Priya: Okay, that helps. 350 qps and mixed sequence lengths, okay. Is model residency an option? Do you need the models and logs to stay in your VPC/on-prem?
[01:33] Aisha: Yes, data residency and not having raw logs leave our VPC is a requirement for a subset of customers. We also need KMS integration for keys and audit logs for every inference request.
[01:43] Jordan: Great - sounds like Dedicated or Private would be the right fit. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools with isolation at the tenant level and VPC peering; Private gives you an on-prem control plane but is heavier to set up. For Dedicated, you can get private networking and customer-managed KMS.
[01:58] Marcus: What's the difference technically between Dedicated and Private in your stack?
[02:02] Diego: Great question. Dedicated is our reserved capacity running in the cloud under your account with strict tenancy boundaries, VPC peering, and key-level access controls. Private is a full control plane we deliver - can be in your VPC or on-prem - where you run the control-plane components. The runtime is the same but deployment model differs. Some customers start on Dedicated then move to Private later.
[02:20] Evelyn: Good to know. For Dedicated, we need guaranteed throughput during marketing spikes; can you talk about burst capacity?
[02:27] Priya: Sure. We offer a baseline of reserved GPUs that guarantee throughput. Then we have burst capacity options - temporary capacity from a shared pool or short-term provisioning of additional nodes. Burst is subject to availability and pricing; we can also architect intake throttling and pre-warming of KV cache to reduce cold-start penalties.
[02:43] Aisha: Pre-warming KV cache - do you mean the key value cache is warmed across the cluster? We have large context keys, worried about memory pressure.
[02:50] Diego: Right, so our runtime supports prefix caching and shared KV cache per model shard. It's not perfect but it significantly reduces repeated autoreads for chat-like flows. We also recommend quantized weights to reduce memory footprint - 8-bit or 4-bit where acceptable. Note: sometimes customers hear K V cash in transcripts - sorry for that - but it's KV cache.
[03:09] Marcus: On the quantization note - what are the trade-offs we should expect on quality vs performance?
[03:13] Priya: Generally 8-bit gives near-native quality with 1.5-2x throughput improvement. 4-bit can give larger memory savings and throughput gains but sometimes requires additional calibration and can introduce minor regressions on some prompt sets. We typically recommend you start with 8-bit and validate with your eval set. Redwood Optimize can run regressions against your prompts.
[03:33] Evelyn: That sounds reasonable. For capacity sizing, we were thinking about 4x A100s to start and add more as needed. What kind of qps does 4x A100 handle for a 34B model at 320 token avg?
[03:44] Priya: Ballpark - with batching and 8-bit quant, 4x A100 could handle roughly 150-250 qps depending on batching policy and latency target. For 350 qps with tight latency you'd be looking at 8x A100 or a mixed pool with higher-end GPUs plus aggressive batching. We should run a benchmark with your prompts to be precise.
[04:06] Marcus: How does Redwood handle autoscaling? We want guaranteed baseline but also autoscale for unpredictable peaks.
[04:12] Jordan: We provide configurable autoscaling policies for Dedicated: you define min reserved capacity, a target utilization threshold, scale-up cooldowns, and max burst. Autoscaling can be reactive (queue/latency based) and proactive (scheduled or predictive based on traffic patterns). For critical bursts you can also reserve burst capacity as an addon.
[04:31] Aisha: Any cold start concerns when scaling up? If a new node comes up, how long until it serves traffic at low latency?
[04:37] Diego: Good point. Cold starts depend on model size and whether weights are loaded in quantized form. We use async prefetch and warm snapshots; typical cold start to ready-serving is ~30-120s for large models. For absolute low-latency needs, we recommend some baseline headroom plus warm pool or pre-warmed instances.
[04:55] Evelyn: For security/compliance, we need SOC2, ISO attestation, full audit trails per inference request, and SSO provisioning. Can Redwood accommodate?
[05:02] Jordan: Yes. We can provide SOC2 docs, our security whitepaper, and we support SSO/SAML, RBAC, and auditable logs. For Dedicated we can enable customer KMS and ensure logs are pushed to your log collector. We'll share the docs after the call.
[05:16] Tom: Procurement - what's the typical contract length and cancellation for Dedicated? We have budget cycles in January and need to keep options open.
[05:22] Jordan: Dedicated usually has reserved monthly or annual commits for predictability. We can provide a pilot month-to-month for the initial benchmark/pilot, then transition to a 12-month reserved commit for better pricing. We'll outline that in the SOW.
[05:34] Marcus: Network - we will need VPC peering and egress controls. Can we restrict egress to internal endpoints?
[05:39] Priya: Yes, VPC peering and private endpoints are supported. You can restrict egress, and we integrate with customer-managed KMS. Some customers also deploy NAT/firewall rules on their side for additional controls.
[05:48] Aisha: Observability - we need per-call latency and token cost visibility and tracing into our app. Do you expose per-route dashboards?
[05:55] Diego: Yup - Redwood Console gives per-route/model dashboards, token-level cost breakdowns, traces, and error analysis. We can also push metrics to your Prometheus/Grafana stack.
[06:05] Evelyn: On canaries and rollouts - we want gradual rollouts and automatic fallback if quality regresses. How mature are your rollout tools?
[06:11] Priya: We support canary percentages, A/B testing by route, and automatic fallback policies to a lower-cost or more stable variant if errors or latencies spike. We also tie to Redwood Optimize so you can detect quality regressions against eval prompt sets.
[06:24] Marcus: For scaling expected costs, can you provide a simple TCO - like cost per 1k tokens for the dedicated baseline vs hosted?
[06:31] Jordan: We'll provide a detailed cost model in the follow-up. Quick note: dedicated tends to have lower per-token cost at higher sustained throughput because you amortize reserved GPUs; hosted is simpler with no ops but can be more expensive for heavy steady usage. We'll include sample scenarios in the pricing doc.
[06:46] Evelyn: Great. For the benchmark, what instrumentation do you need from us?
[06:50] Priya: Sample prompt set including short/long contexts, expected QPS profile (arrival distribution), auth tokens if any, and details about any custom preprocessing steps. Also we'd like a list of success criteria: latency SLO, quality thresholds, and cost targets.
[07:04] Evelyn: We'll share that. We also have some compliance customers who need logs to be purged after 30 days - is retention configurable?
[07:10] Diego: Retention is configurable in Dedicated; we can support shorter retention windows and purge policies to meet regulatory needs.
[07:18] Aisha: One more infra question: do you support node-level placement to avoid noisy neighbors? For example we want true single-tenant GPU nodes for a subset of workloads.
[07:26] Jordan: Yes, as part of Dedicated you can opt for single-tenant nodes (physical or isolated GPU pools) for an additional cost. That ensures no tenant sharing on those GPUs.
[07:36] Tom: If we go for single-tenant nodes, how does that change procurement? Need to know lead times.
[07:41] Jordan: Lead times depend on region and availability; typical lead times for dedicated single-tenant provisioning are 2-6 weeks. We'll capture that timeline in the SOW.
[07:51] Marcus: Regarding model updates and KV cache invalidation - how are rolling updates handled to avoid cache thrash?
[07:58] Priya: We support rolling rollouts with staged traffic shift and KV cache warming. You can pin model versions and we support atomic switchovers to reduce cache misses. For big model changes there will be a period of warming - we can coordinate pre-warm runs.
[08:12] Evelyn: Any recommended quantization profile for our lodestar-34b? We care about quality on financial language.
[08:18] Diego: For finance-specific language I'd recommend 8-bit first and test. If after regression evaluation you're comfortable, try a tuned 4-bit with outlier handling. Redwood Optimize can recommend quant profiles per workload.
[08:30] Marcus: Let's talk numbers - if we wanted to support 350 qps peak with p95 under 350 ms for average prompts, it sounds like 8x A100 or equivalent. Does Redwood support mixed pools so we can have some large GPUs for heavy flows and smaller ones for background jobs?
[08:43] Priya: Yes, mixed pools are supported. You can route traffic by policy; critical routes go to high-performance nodes, background batch jobs can run on cheaper instances. Smart routing and automated fallback helps here.
[08:55] Evelyn: For bursting, if shared pool is exhausted, do we get queued requests or fallback to hosted?
[09:00] Jordan: You can configure either behavior. Options: queue with backpressure, fallback to hosted API (if acceptable), or degrade to smaller model variant. We'll design a policy based on your tolerance.
[09:10] Marcus: Let's set out clear success criteria for the pilot: 1) deliver 300 qps sustained for 1 hour with p95 < 350ms on avg prompts, 2) confirm KMS integration and logs sent to our collector, 3) validate 8-bit quant quality within X% measured by our eval prompts.
[09:25] Evelyn: Yes, that aligns. We also want to validate canary rollback works end-to-end.
[09:30] Priya: Perfect. For timeline, if you share the prompt set and traffic profile by 12/23, we can scope the benchmark and get a pilot running by first week of January.
[09:39] Tom: Procurement - we'll aim to have initial PO ready by Jan 10, pending pricing.
[09:43] Jordan: Sounds good. Any other questions?
[09:46] Aisha: One more - encryption in transit and at rest? We require TLS 1.2+ and all storage encrypted with customer KMS.
[09:53] Diego: We support TLS 1.2/1.3 and customer-managed KMS for at-rest encryption. We'll include technical specifics in the security pack.
[09:59] Marcus: Ok thanks.
[10:01] Jordan: Quick recap - we'll send preliminary pricing for a 4x and 8x A100 config plus single-tenant option, include burst pricing and pilot pricing. Priya will prepare benchmark plan and prompt set template. Aisha will share traffic numbers and infra diagrams. Tom will outline procurement timeline. We'll target the benchmark kickoff first week of Jan.
[10:20] Evelyn: That works for us. Thanks all.
[10:22] Tom: Thanks.
[10:24] Jordan: Great - we'll follow up with the docs and SOW draft.

Notes (auto-gen-like imperfections): there were a few mis-attributed lines where speaker labels were noisy, and some tech words transcribed as similar-sounding variants (e.g., K V cash, A hundred GPUs).

End of transcript.
